items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: like if I walked into the club, you know, and there were a couple of hundred people there, he would say “good evening I’m Joel Dorn and I’m here to entertain you.”

ctx.x: But that’s what — when you went to a club, you know, like for instance I saw Joe fifty times in Philly. Because he always played Philly once a year, he played Showboat or Pep’s. And he was a charming entertainer. And he kidded around with the audience and he knew people in each city. Let me tell you how smart Joe was. Whenever I would walk into the club, I usually caught the last set ‘cause I got off the air at one and the last set

was at one twenty. And you know, on the weekends if it was crowded, he knew how to work disc jockeys, so he always came up — nobody said “Joe Williams,” the trio played, he walked out, he would go into a song and then he would say “good evening I’m Joseph Goreed Williams.” He had this thing, I’m Joe Williams, I’m from Chicago, I’m here to entertain you. But if there was a disc jockey in the room he would come out and when he finished his first number, like if I walked into the club, you know, and there were a…

I remember that moment the first time I brought those tapes down and we put them on. I said I knew I found the right guy ‘cause you like jumped out of your seat and said, “do you know what you have here?” I really remember that, it was funny. Then Gene Paul said, as we were going through those things, he said, “this is better than dinosaur bones.”
